name: chapter_section_screen
description: Post-draft Jev screen, one call per section. Only questions that proved reliable on a test chapter. Thresholds tuned on jev-1.13.0; re-tune before changing model.

session_content_conflict.instructions: Does `section_text` say which subject or class is taught in a named session or time slot listed in `bible.timetable` that is different from what `bible.timetable` lists for that session?

criteria.true: A session is described as teaching a subject that bible.timetable does not list for it.
criteria.false: No session content is stated, or it matches bible.timetable.

pov_head_hop.instructions: The narration must stay in close third person inside the POV character's head only (`bible.pov`). Does the narration in `section_text` directly state what a character other than the POV character feels, thinks, knows, notices or decides inside, rather than showing it through that character's words or visible actions?

criteria.true: At least one narration sentence reports another character's inner state as fact (e.g. 'Kit felt nervous', 'She knew he was lying').
criteria.false: Only the POV character's inner states are narrated; other characters are seen from outside.

ai_mirrored_lines.instructions: Does `section_text` contain two or more sentences or clauses built as a mirrored pair, repeating the same opening words or structure for rhetorical effect?

criteria.true: A repeated-structure pair such as 'He had wanted the house. He had wanted it, and he had wanted it badly.' appears.
criteria.false: No sentence repeats the structure or opening words of a neighbor for rhetorical effect.

ai_rule_of_three.instructions: Does `section_text` contain a decorative list of exactly three parallel items (nouns, noun phrases, or clauses) used for rhythm, such as 'the A, the B and the C' or 'A, and B, and C'?

criteria.true: A three-item parallel list used for rhythm appears.
criteria.false: No three-item rhythmic list appears; lists are of two items or are plain inventories required by the action.

ai_tidy_closer.instructions: Does `section_text` end (in its last paragraph) on a neat, aphoristic, or summarizing line that tells the reader what the scene meant?

criteria.true: The last paragraph sums up or moralizes, e.g. a crisp epigram or a 'they had seen...' summary.
criteria.false: The section ends on action, dialogue, or a concrete image without summing up its meaning.

ai_packed_noun.instructions: Does narration in `section_text` use a short noun that never gets a referent, so the reader cannot tell what concrete thing it names (for example 'the streak', 'the pull', 'the feed', or 'the signal')?

criteria.true: A short loaded noun stands in for a thing the sentence never names.
criteria.false: Each noun has a clear referent in the sentence or the one before it.

ai_hedge_stack.instructions: Does narration in `section_text` stack hedges (two or more of may, might, could, possibly, potentially, perhaps) so the action has no clear outcome?

criteria.true: A narration sentence stacks two or more hedges.
criteria.false: Hedges are absent, or a single hedge is ordinary dialogue.

ai_soft_contrast.instructions: Does narration in `section_text` use a soft contrast that names a rejected alternative, such as 'X, not Y', 'rather than X, Y', or 'instead of X, Y'?

criteria.true: Narration names the thing by rejecting an alternative.
criteria.false: The narration states the thing directly, or the contrast is inside quoted dialogue.

ai_unclear_agency.instructions: Does narration in `section_text` leave who does what to whom unclear, or open on a pronoun when more than one character could be the referent?

criteria.true: A narration sentence hides the agent, or a pronoun has two possible referents.
criteria.false: Each narration sentence has a clear agent and a single referent for each pronoun.

ai_polished_intro.instructions: This section opens a scene or chapter. Does it open as a polished thesis, definition, or summary of the place or situation, instead of inside a concrete moment, action, or line?

criteria.true: The opening summarises or defines before anything happens.
criteria.false: The opening is already inside an action, a line of dialogue, or a concrete sensory detail.

ai_parallel_list_ending.instructions: This section closes a scene or chapter. Does it end on a tidy parallel list: three or more sentences with the same opening, an 'N things/reasons/habits' list, or a closing tricolon summary?

criteria.true: The close is an anaphora, an 'N things' list, or a tricolon summary.
criteria.false: The close is an action, an image, or a line of dialogue.

ya_appropriate.instructions: Is `section_text` appropriate for a young-adult novel for readers aged 12 and up (no explicit sex, no graphic gore, no strong profanity)?

criteria.false: Contains content unsuitable for readers 12 and up.

plan_beat.instructions: Which planned beat from `scene_plan.beats` does `section_text` mainly show? Pick 'none' if it shows none of them.

thresholds._notes: flag_with_code_at: lower bar used only when the matching code check (screen.CODE_LINK) also fired in the section. ai_polished_intro is asked on the first section of a scene only; ai_parallel_list_ending on the last section only. The six de-AI questions ride the existing per-section call and are omitted when screen.deai_questions is false.

bible_hint.ai_tidy_closer: Style lock: no tidy morals or summarizing closers.
bible_hint.ai_packed_noun: Name the thing. No packed noun standing in for an unnamed contrast.
bible_hint.ai_hedge_stack: No hedge stacks. Say who does what.
bible_hint.ai_soft_contrast: State the thing directly. No 'X, not Y' or 'rather than X, Y' in narration.
bible_hint.ai_unclear_agency: Clear referents and clear agency. Who does what to whom.
bible_hint.ai_polished_intro: Start inside a concrete moment. No thesis-style scene opener.
bible_hint.ai_parallel_list_ending: End on an action, an image, or a line. No parallel-list closer.
